explanation:
[EFFECT]
Wind speed has a mostly downward effect on predicted bike demand as it increases. At very low wind speeds (roughly below 10 km/h), the contribution is slightly positive, giving demand a tiny boost. From moderate speeds onward (~17 km/h and above), the effect turns increasingly negative, with the strongest suppression at the highest wind speeds (~54 km/h), where predicted demand is reduced by about 30% compared to calm conditions.

[IMPORTANCE]
Wind speed is ranked 8th out of 9 features in importance (score: 0.014), making it one of the weakest drivers of predicted demand in the model. Its influence is real but small compared to factors like hour of day or temperature.

[RECOMMENDATION]
On particularly windy days (speeds above ~30–40 km/h), you can expect a moderate dip in rentals, so it may be reasonable to slightly reduce bike rebalancing efforts or staffing on such days, though the effect is modest compared to other factors.
